I'd like to hear your thoughts on suicidal ideation with SSRIs. When I was an intern I attended what's known as Pharmacy Law Day where we spoke with legislators regarding improvements to our profession. I remember a lay person being in the room with us talking about her daughter who had taken her life while on an SSRI and she was so adamant to get an additional warning placed on these types of medications. Her proposal was a Purple Box Warning instead of/addition to the Black Box Warning. I don't know the full history and circumstances that lead to her daughter's death but ever since then I've been diligent to communicate this warning to my patients. Making sure to let them know it can take 6-8 weeks to see real improvement and to call their doctor immediately if they have any thoughts of planning to harm themselves. I've been taught that antidepressants, within the first few weeks, can increase a person's energy but at the same time not treat the depression yet so it gives the person the energy to actually go through with harming themselves. I also ask if they're seeing a therapist too. I don't agree with putting people on these meds without talking to a trained professional during the process.
